what_it_does: Zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) are a cryptographic technique that lets one party convince another that a computation was done correctly without revealing any of the private inputs — think of proving you know a secret password without ever showing it. A popular modern variant called a zkSNARK (a compact, efficiently-checkable proof) is increasingly used in privacy-preserving blockchains and secure computing, but generating these proofs is extremely slow, especially for operations like large matrix multiplications (multiplying big grids of numbers together, a core building block of AI and many algorithms). This paper introduces zkVC, a system that speeds up ZKP generation specifically for matrix multiplies. It proposes two algorithmic ideas: a 'Constraint-reduced Polynomial Circuit' that reduces the number of mathematical constraints the prover must satisfy, and a 'Prefix-Sum Query' method for more efficient aggregation of results. The abstract does not provide benchmark numbers or describe a hardware implementation, so the extent of the speedup is not yet clear.
